# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Monday, November 2, 2026

*Monday edition, compiled before the market opens. Equity, index, rupee and flow numbers are Friday 30 October closes because markets were shut over the weekend; gold and Brent are as of this morning. Muthoot Fincorp Ltd is a separate company from Muthoot Finance Ltd; Muthoot Finance appears here as a listed gold-loan lender.*

---

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

**1. Muthoot Finance explains its Stage 3 jump: short-tenure and monthly-EMI gold loans are tripping into overdue buckets**
On its Q2 call, Muthoot Finance said Stage 3 rose to ₹7,267 crore (3.87% of loan assets) from ₹2,977 crore a year ago, and Stage 2 (31–89 days) jumped to ₹23,467 crore from ₹534 crore. MD Alexander George Muthoot tied it to the shorter-tenure and interest-servicing schemes that followed RBI's gold-loan directions (effective 1 April 2026). Management said about ₹3,000 crore of the Stage 3 pool is second or third accounts of borrowers whose other loans are still in Stage 1 or 2, clubbed together because it classifies borrower-wise. It quoted LTVs of 53% on Stage 3 and 72% on Stage 2, and said auction is the last resort. The article also notes Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance flagged higher gold-loan slippages after the same shift. ([Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/news/short-tenure-loans-monthly-emis-drive-up-gold-loan-npas-muthoot-finance-md/4374640/))
> **Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:** Muthoot Fincorp is subject to the same April 2026 gold-loan directions, so analysts are likely to read its Q2 Stage 2 and Stage 3 figures against this disclosure.

**2. Bank lending to NBFCs up 41.8% year on year in September**
Bank credit to NBFCs reached ₹22.53 lakh crore in September, up 41.8% from a year earlier (3.7% growth a year ago). NBFCs now make up about 35% of bank lending to services (₹64.9 lakh crore, +28.3%). Lending to HFCs grew 19.7%; overall bank credit grew 19.4% to ₹229.95 lakh crore. ETBFSI raises the question of whether some of this is circular credit growth. ([ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/bank-lending-to-nbfcs-surges-42-raising-questions-over-circular-credit-growth/135441224); underlying data: [RBI sectoral deployment, Sept 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63891))
> **Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:** Bank lines are a funding source for NBFCs including Muthoot Fincorp; RBI raised risk weights on bank lending to NBFCs after a similar surge in November 2023 ([RBI/2023-24/85](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12567&Mode=0)), so any repeat would affect the cost of that funding across the sector.

**3. Nomura's bear case: weak monsoons could hit rural NBFC books**
The south-west monsoon ended 13% short; the north-east monsoon was 54% below normal over 1–24 October, with South Peninsula 31% short; rabi sowing is down 37% year on year. Nomura's bear case assumes a 7.25% risk-free rate (vs 6.25%) and halved insurance fee income from FY28. Its preferred names are Piramal, Tata Capital, Aadhar Housing and Bajaj Finance; it notes CreditAccess Grameen trades below previous-crisis multiples. ([ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/nbfcs-brace-for-rural-loan-stress-as-drought-and-weak-monsoon-hit-farm-incomes/135441225))
> **Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:** Muthoot Fincorp is headquartered in Kerala and lends heavily in south India, so a weak north-east monsoon over the South Peninsula touches the region where much of its gold-loan book sits.

---

## 🏢 Muthoot Fincorp in the market

- **Tranche I public NCD issue (open 23 Oct – 5 Nov 2026).** Bids stood at 1.86 times the ₹200 crore base issue as of 17:00 IST on Friday 30 October: retail 1.60×, HNI 2.56×, non-institutional 1.29×, QIB 0.00×. The issue size including the green-shoe option is ₹500 crore. No bidding took place over the weekend. ([Chittorgarh](https://www.chittorgarh.com/bond/muthoot-fincorp-tranche-i-ncd-october-2026/399/))
- **Scheduled dates.** Allotment on 9 November and BSE listing on 10 November, per the issue schedule. ([Groww](https://groww.in/bonds/ipo/muthoot-fincorp-tranche-i-ncd-october-2026))
- **Ratings.** The Tranche I NCDs are rated Crisil AA/Stable and Brickwork AA+/Stable. ([Chittorgarh](https://www.chittorgarh.com/bond/muthoot-fincorp-tranche-i-ncd-october-2026/399/))
- **Subsidiary.** Muthoot Microfin, Muthoot Fincorp's listed microfinance subsidiary, holds its Q2 board meeting on 5 November ([StockFin](https://www.stockfin.ai/news/MUTHOOTMF/2026-10-23/board-meeting)). Its provisional Q2 business update is covered in the sector deep dive below.

---

## 📈 Market & Stock Summary

Friday 30 October: Sensex closed 308.49 points (0.42%) higher at 74,459.53 and Nifty 50 rose 116.35 points (0.51%) to 23,053.10; both gained nearly 2% for the week ([BusinessLine](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/sensex-nifty50-today-stock-market-highlights-30th-october-2026/article71640574.ece)). Nifty Financial Services was flat (+0.03%) at 24,712.20, but Nifty Financial Services Ex-Bank fell 1.04% to 28,504.70, so non-bank financials lagged ([NSE index closes](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/indices/ind_close_all_30102026.csv)).

Gold-loan and diversified NBFC stocks sold off on Friday: IIFL Finance −6.15%, Manappuram Finance −4.34%, Muthoot Finance −3.54% (ahead of its Q2 numbers), Shriram Finance −2.13%; Bajaj Finance was flat ([NSE bhavcopy](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/products/content/sec_bhavdata_full_30102026.csv)). FIIs were net buyers of ₹3,598.54 crore and DIIs net sellers of ₹817.51 crore, provisional ([CNBC-TV18](https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/fiis-return-to-buying-indian-stocks-with-rs3599-crore-inflows-diis-turn-net-sellers-20023622.htm)). For the week, FIIs net bought ₹6,305 crore, ending a 10-week selling streak ([Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/can-nifty-sensex-extend-gains-after-rallying-up-to-2-last-week-4-factors-to-watch-on-monday/articleshow/135419919.cms)).

This week: US midterm elections (Tuesday), US jobs data, PMI prints, oil and more Q2 results. Moneycontrol puts Nifty support at 22,800–22,900 and resistance at 23,150–23,200 ([Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/dalal-street-week-ahead-us-midterm-elections-jobs-data-q2-earnings-pmi-numbers-oil-prices-among-10-key-factors-to-watch-14065576.html)).

This morning, Brent fell 1.4% to $111.84 by 0011 GMT as Iran–Qatar talks ran into a third day; OPEC+ held December targets ([Moneycontrol/Reuters](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/commodities/oil-prices-fall-over-1-as-iran-peace-talks-gather-pace-brent-slips-below-112-14065629.html)). Spot gold was $3,908.50/oz, up 0.23%, at 01:29 UTC ([gold-pricex](https://gold-pricex.com/gold-price-today)).

> **Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:** Gold steadied near $3,900 after last week's fall, which keeps collateral values for gold lenders, Muthoot Fincorp included, broadly unchanged since Friday.

---

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

- No new RBI notifications since 30 October (UAPA Taliban-list update, already logged) ([RBI notifications](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx)).
- No new SEBI circulars since 30 October ([SEBI circulars](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=1&ssid=7&smid=0)); no new IBBI circulars since 30 October ([IBBI circulars](https://ibbi.gov.in/en/legal-framework/circulars)).
- Banks are asking for an extension of CGFMU, the microloan credit-guarantee scheme that ended on 31 March 2026 ([Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/banks-seek-microloan-guarantee-extension/articleshow/135435172.cms)).

More detail on today's Rules page.

---

## 💰 Financial Results & Performance

**LIC Housing Finance raises lending rates by 25 bp.** About 35% of the book resets from 1 November and 65% from 1 January. Q2 NIM was 2.58% (down 4 bp), PAT ₹1,506 crore (+12%) and disbursements ₹18,127 crore (+11%). ([Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/lichf-bets-on-diversification-to-drive-growth/articleshow/135436287.cms))
> A large lender passing on rate increases indicates funding costs are still rising after RBI's October hike.

For the Muthoot Finance Q2 numbers, see item 1 above.

---

No significant developments today.

## 📉 NPA & Asset Quality

- Muthoot Finance Stage 2 at ₹23,467 crore vs ₹534 crore a year ago; Stage 3 at 3.87% ([Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/news/short-tenure-loans-monthly-emis-drive-up-gold-loan-npas-muthoot-finance-md/4374640/)). See item 1.
- Rural stress risk from the weak north-east monsoon ([ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/nbfcs-brace-for-rural-loan-stress-as-drought-and-weak-monsoon-hit-farm-incomes/135441225)). See item 3.

---

No significant developments today.

## 🏭 Sector Deep Dive — Monday: Microfinance & SHG lending

**Where the sector stands.** Sa-Dhan's Bharat Microfinance Report says the industry book shrank 11% in FY26 to ₹3.34 trillion, PAR 180+ rose to 17.04% from 10.67%, and active accounts fell 21% to 10.40 crore. The report sees early signs of recovery, but legacy bad loans still weigh ([Mint](https://www.livemint.com/news/microfinance-shows-early-recovery-signs-but-legacy-bad-loans-weigh-on-sector-11791450920201.html)).

**The guardrails.** MFIN's rules cap a borrower at three lenders, total MFI debt within ₹2 lakh, and no fresh loans to anyone 60+ days past due. Industry leaders are pushing diversification into secured and individual loans ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/specials/bs-events/microfinance-lenders-eye-diversification-as-sector-recovers-industry-leaders-126102600830_1.html)).

**The guarantee gap.** CGFMU ended on 31 March 2026, and banks want it extended. IDFC First's ₹6,825 crore MFI book is 97% covered and AU SFB's is 99% covered, which shows how much lenders leaned on it ([Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/banks-seek-microloan-guarantee-extension/articleshow/135435172.cms)).

**The new risk.** The weak north-east monsoon and 37% lower rabi sowing hit exactly the rural borrowers MFIs serve; Nomura notes CreditAccess Grameen trades below previous-crisis multiples ([ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/nbfcs-brace-for-rural-loan-stress-as-drought-and-weak-monsoon-hit-farm-incomes/135441225)).

**Muthoot Microfin.** Muthoot Microfin, Muthoot Fincorp's listed microfinance subsidiary, reported Q2 FY27 AUM of ₹15,323 crore (+22%), disbursements of ₹2,900 crore (+28%), collection efficiency of 98.11% and cost of funds of 9.93%. Its JLG to non-JLG mix moved to 69:31 from 83:17 in March, and it disbursed ₹453 crore of gold loans under a referral and co-lending arrangement with Muthoot Fincorp. These are provisional, unaudited business-update figures ([CNBC-TV18](https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/muthoot-microfin-share-price-q2-biz-update-aum-growth-gold-loans-sme-jlg-mix-cost-of-funds-drop-20007277.htm)).

> **Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:** Muthoot Microfin's results are consolidated into Muthoot Fincorp's, so south-India drought stress on joint-liability loans, with CGFMU cover lapsed, would show up in the group's consolidated credit costs.

No new RBI/SEBI circulars or regulatory changes related to NBFCs were found today.

Nothing has been published by RBI, SEBI or IBBI since the 30 Oct batch, which is already in the log.

### What is in the market that is *not* an NBFC circular

| **Muthoot Finance Q2 call.** Stage 3 ₹7,267 cr (3.87%) vs ₹2,977 cr; Stage 2 ₹23,467 cr vs ₹534 cr. The MD blames short-tenure and interest-servicing schemes that followed the 1 April 2026 gold-loan directions; about ₹3,000 cr of Stage 3 is borrower-wise clubbing; Stage 3 LTV 53%, Stage 2 LTV 72%. | Management commentary, not regulation. [Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/news/short-tenure-loans-monthly-emis-drive-up-gold-loan-npas-muthoot-finance-md/4374640/) |

# 📋 NBFC Weekly Analysis: Week of 26 October – 1 November 2026

*Published Monday, 2 November 2026 (IST). Covers trading sessions Mon 26 to Fri 30 October, plus Muthoot Finance's Q2 on Saturday 31 October and weekend news. Muthoot Fincorp Ltd is a Middle Layer NBFC with unlisted equity and listed NCDs. Muthoot Finance Ltd is a separate, listed company; none of its numbers are Muthoot Fincorp's.*

## Executive Summary

- **The gold-loan stress story got its biggest data point yet, and it came from a peer.** Muthoot Finance (not Muthoot Fincorp) reported standalone Stage 3 of 3.87%, up from 2.28% in June, and Stage 2 of ₹23,467 cr against ₹534 cr a year ago. Its MD blamed the short-tenure and monthly-servicing schemes that followed RBI's 1 April 2026 gold-lending directions, and said about ₹3,000 cr of Stage 3 is borrower-wise clubbing of accounts that are otherwise current ([ET](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/earnings/muthoot-finance-q2-cons-profit-jumps-36-yoy-to-rs-3278-crore/articleshow/135401237.cms), [Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/news/short-tenure-loans-monthly-emis-drive-up-gold-loan-npas-muthoot-finance-md/4374640/)). Shriram, Bajaj Finance and Piramal had already flagged the same thing.
- **Gold fell again, hard.** Spot gold lost 3.04% on Friday alone to $3,899.33, its first close under $3,900 since mid-July, and ended the week about 3% lower. MCX December gold finished Friday's session at ₹1,38,419/10g ([CNBC-TV18](https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/commodities/gold-silver-prices-crash-mcx-gold-plunges-to-rs-1-lakh-silver-falls-to-rs-1-lakh-per-kg-20023794.htm), [ET](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/commoditysummary/symbol-GOLD.cms)). Listed gold lenders gave back most of Thursday's rally on Friday.
- **Bond yields finally broke their losing run, but lenders are still raising rates.** The 10-year G-sec fell about 6 bps on the week to 7.414%, ending a 10-week selloff ([ET](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/bonds/india-bonds-buckle-for-fourth-straight-month-on-oils-climb/articleshow/135361502.cms)). Even so, Tata Capital, PNB Housing and LIC Housing all announced lending-rate increases from 1 November, and ABCL, Chola and Five-Star each put a number on rising funding costs.
- **Banks are pouring money into NBFCs.** Bank credit to NBFCs was up 41.8% year on year in September to ₹22.53 lakh cr ([ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/bank-lending-to-nbfcs-surges-42-raising-questions-over-circular-credit-growth/135441224)). That helps funding now, but it is the kind of number that has drawn RBI risk-weight action before (November 2023).
- **Muthoot Fincorp's week: Tranche I bids went from 0.55× to 1.86×.** About ₹372 cr was bid against the ₹500 cr full issue size (₹200 cr base + ₹300 cr green shoe), with bidding closing Thu 5 Nov ([Chittorgarh](https://www.chittorgarh.com/bond/muthoot-fincorp-tranche-i-ncd-october-2026/399/)). CareEdge Global moved Muthoot Fincorp's subsidiary Muthoot Microfin to a Positive outlook and cited support from Muthoot Fincorp by name ([EquityBulls](https://www.equitybulls.com/news/377689/muthoot-microfin-earns-positive-outlook-from-careedge-global-on-stronger-asset-q)).

## 🏛️ Regulatory & Policy Watch

A quiet week for new rules. Nothing RBI issued changes how an NBFC lends, prices or provisions. The work this week was in the sanctions file and in reading what the April gold-loan directions are doing to peer books.

**1. Three UAPA Section 51A circulars addressed to NBFCs (27 and 30 Oct).** `RBI/2026-27/301` removed 3 entries from the UNSC ISIL & Al-Qaida list, `/302` amended 3 entries on the same list, and `/303` amended 5 entries on the Taliban list. All three refer to Chapter IX of the KYC Directions, 2025 ([RBI /301](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13747&Mode=0), [RBI /302](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13748&Mode=0), [RBI /303](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13749&Mode=0)).
- *Direct impact:* same-day screening updates. Amendments matter more than removals, because a new alias or passport number can create a fresh hit on an existing customer.
- *Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:* compliance work for its AML screening; no direct financial impact.

**2. RBI sectoral credit data for September (30 Oct).** Non-food bank credit +19.1%, services +28.3%, with NBFCs among the "buoyant" segments. Bank loans against gold jewellery slowed versus last year but "remained strong" ([RBI PR 2026-2027/1412](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63891)). ETBFSI's read of the same data puts bank credit to NBFCs at +41.8% ([ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/bank-lending-to-nbfcs-surges-42-raising-questions-over-circular-credit-growth/135441224)).
- *Second order:* in November 2023 RBI raised risk weights on bank exposure to NBFCs after a similar run. Nothing has been announced this time, but the 2–4 Dec policy and the next Financial Stability Report are the places a signal would show up.
- *Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:* bank term loans are one of its funding sources, so any supervisory tightening on bank lending to NBFCs would bear on the cost of renewals.

**3. SEBI and IBBI housekeeping.** SEBI gave debenture trustees until 27 Apr 2027 to ring-fence non-SEBI business ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/oct-2026/extension-of-timeline-for-compliance-with-terms-and-conditions-by-debenture-trustees-dts-for-carrying-out-activities-outside-the-purview-of-sebi_105454.html)), extended digital-accessibility deadlines for its regulated entities to 31 Jan 2027 ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/oct-2026/extension-of-timeline-with-respect-to-compliance-of-digital-accessibility-circulars_105523.html)), and eased FPI KYC review periodicity. IBBI issued two real-estate CIRP circulars, `IBBI/CIRP/109/2026` and `/110/2026` ([IBBI](https://ibbi.gov.in/en/legal-framework/circulars)).
- *Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:* none directly. Muthoot Fincorp is a debt issuer rather than a SEBI regulated entity, and it participates as a financial creditor in CIRP. The creditor-led CIIRP route under the IBC (Amendment) Act 2026 is still not notified ([NCLT commencement notification](https://nclt.gov.in/sites/default/files/Act%26rules/The%20Insolvency%20and%20Bankruptcy%20Code%20%28Amendment%29%20Act%2C%202026%20Enforment%20Date%20Notification.pdf)).

**4. Not a regulation, but it reads like one: the April gold-loan directions are now visible in Stage 2 and 3.** Muthoot Finance's MD described the 1 April 2026 rules as a learning curve for the company and its customers that will stabilise over a few quarters ([NDTV Profit](https://www.ndtvprofit.com/markets/muthoot-finance-q2-results-profit-rises-27-to-rs-2-977-crore-revises-gold-loan-growth-guidance-for-fy27-12263278)).
- *Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:* it is subject to the same directions, and its Q2 results (LODR deadline 14 Nov) are likely to be compared with this print, particularly how much of any Stage 3 movement is rule-driven or borrower-wise clubbing versus collection stress.

**5. Still pending.** The revolving-credit draft (6 Aug) and Interest Rate Directions draft (12 Aug) have not been finalised; RBI's latest draft is still 11 Sep ([RBI drafts](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/DraftNotificationsGuildelines.aspx)). RBI has described the revolving-credit restriction as a clarification of existing rules ([Mint](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/rbi-says-nbfc-ban-on-revolving-credit-is-a-clarification-not-a-new-rule-11791378140568.html)). The SEBI Credit Risk-o-Meter goes live on 21 Nov and will apply to debt offer documents filed after that date, including Muthoot Fincorp's ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/oct-2026/introduction-of-credit-risk-o-meter-as-an-additional-disclosure-mechanism-for-debt-securities_105081.html)).

## 💳 Credit & Lending Trends

Surplus liquidity fell from ₹4.38 lakh cr on 1 Oct to ₹2.42 lakh cr on 15 Oct ([BusinessLine](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/deposits-and-advances-of-banks-decline-in-the-first-fortnight-of-oct-2026/article71646237.ece)).

## ⚠️ Asset Quality Deep Dive

**Gold loans: the mechanics are now on the record.** Here is what the week added:
- **Muthoot Finance:** Stage 3 ₹7,267 cr (3.87%), Stage 2 ₹23,467 cr. About ₹3,000 cr of Stage 3 is second or third accounts of borrowers whose other loans are current, pulled in by borrower-wise classification. LTV on Stage 3 is 53% and on Stage 2 is 72%, and auction is "the last resort" ([Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/news/short-tenure-loans-monthly-emis-drive-up-gold-loan-npas-muthoot-finance-md/4374640/)). Cofacto's read of the filing puts the quarter's impairment charge at ₹514.92 cr ([Cofacto](https://cofacto.ai/market-news/muthootfin-q2-fy27-results-analysis)).
- **Shriram:** gold-book GS3 3.12% from 2.57% ([VCCircle/Reuters](https://www.vccircle.com/shriramfinance-joins-peers-in-flagging-stress-in-gold-loans)).
- **Piramal's estimate** that 15–23% of FY26 industry gold disbursements (about ₹4.7 lakh cr) went to borrowers already 90+ DPD elsewhere kept circulating ([Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/commodities/why-are-nbfcs-flagging-stress-in-gold-loans-despite-a-rush-to-expand-14060075.html)).

Two different things are getting lumped together. The first is technical: monthly-servicing products and borrower-wise tagging push loans into Stage 2/3 that are well covered by gold (53% LTV on Stage 3 is a lot of cushion). The second is real: a subset of borrowers were already stretched elsewhere, and a 3% gold fall in a day plus a weak monsoon in the south squeezes exactly those people. The first one fades as customers learn the new servicing rhythm. The second one doesn't.

**Rural and drought stress.** The south-west monsoon ended 13% short, the north-east monsoon was 54% below normal over 1–24 Oct (South Peninsula −31%), and rabi sowing is down 37% YoY ([ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/nbfcs-brace-for-rural-loan-stress-as-drought-and-weak-monsoon-hit-farm-incomes/135441225)). Shriram, M&M Finance and Bajaj Finance are curbing fresh loans in drought districts ([ET](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/nbfcs-curb-fresh-loans-in-rural-markets-as-weak-monsoon-raises-repayment-risks/articleshow/135222291.cms)). Nomura's bear case is built on the same weather stress ([Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/stocks/nomura-flags-four-headwinds-for-nbfcs-prefers-piramal-finance-tata-capital-aadhar-housing-finance-and-bajaj-finance-14064543.html)).

**Elsewhere it's improving.** Chola GS3 3.25% (3.29%), Tata Capital 1.9% with provisions down 16.6%, LIC Housing 2.05%, PNB Housing 0.91%, ABCL credit cost down to 0.92%. In microfinance, Belstar's GNPA is 3.26% (4.58% a year ago) and Spandana is back in profit ([CNBC-TV18](https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/earnings/muthoot-finance-q2-results-net-profit-rises-27-to-rs2978-crore-nii-up-34-beats-estimates-20024053.htm), [ET](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/earnings/spandana-sphoorty-returns-to-profit-at-rs-18-crore-in-q2fy27/articleshow/135369091.cms)). Muthoot Microfin's GNPA was 3.7% at 30 Jun ([EquityBulls](https://www.equitybulls.com/news/377689/muthoot-microfin-earns-positive-outlook-from-careedge-global-on-stronger-asset-q)).

**Provisioning watch:** Five-Star's Stage 3 PCR of 39.49% and Muthoot Finance's reported 11.80% coverage (per Cofacto) are low, though for a gold book a low PCR is defensible because the collateral covers the loan.

**Recoveries and ARCs:** No sourced ARC transaction or recovery-mechanism data was found for this week. Banks are asking for an extension of CGFMU, the microloan credit guarantee that lapsed on 31 Mar 2026; nothing is notified yet ([ET](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/banks-seek-microloan-guarantee-extension/articleshow/135435172.cms)).

## 💻 Digital & Innovation Pulse

- **Cyber fraud at small NBFCs:** about ₹300 cr stolen in two months across roughly 150 complaints, mostly through compromised payment and disbursement APIs. The figure is a sourced estimate, not an official one ([Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/rs-300-crore-stolen-from-small-nbfcs-in-cyberattacks-officials-flag-jamtara-style-fraud-risk-14063062.html)). CERT-In's 9 Oct advisory recommends credential rotation, MFA, maker-checker and payout limits ([CERT-In summary](https://www.compliedai.com/updates/cert-in/ciad-2026-0046-threat-actors-exploiting-payment-and-disbursement-apis-fo-cabo4h)).
- **Digital lenders are growing fast and getting cheaper money.** Kissht doubled PAT on 68% AUM growth; Navi's adjusted 90+ DPD fell to 3.2% from 6.9% and it won an upgrade.
- **Platforms want the balance sheet.** Meesho is moving from lending service provider to owning credit risk, and PhonePe Lending is pushing data-led credit to small-town merchants ([Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/small-town-merchants-to-power-next-phase-of-credit-growth-says-phonepe-lending-ceo-hemant-gala-article-14062444.html)).
- **Product design under the revolving-credit draft:** Bajaj Finance is launching new term-loan variants from 1 Nov ([Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/banks/bajaj-finance-to-introduce-new-term-loan-variants-after-rbi-draft-proposal-on-revolving-credit-ban-14055712.html)); Tata Capital says revolving/flexi products are 3–4% of its AUM.
- **Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp:** the thin-file small-town borrower who takes a gold loan is also the customer these platforms are targeting with unsecured credit. The CERT-In advisory on payment and disbursement APIs applies to any lender that pays out loans through such APIs.

## 💡 Analyst's Take

The signal this week was Muthoot Finance's Stage 2 going from ₹534 cr to ₹23,467 cr. The 3.87% Stage 3 headline matters less. A move that size in a 31–89 day bucket isn't a credit event; it's a servicing pattern changing under new rules. Management's own detail (53% LTV on Stage 3, ₹3,000 cr of clubbed accounts) says the collateral is fine. The question is whether that Stage 2 pool rolls into Stage 3 over the next two quarters or cures. If it cures, Q2 FY27 will look like a one-time reset. If gold keeps falling and the north-east monsoon failure hits farm cash flow in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra, the roll rate goes up just when the cushion is shrinking. Both things are happening at once, and they're easy to confuse.

The rate story is quieter but more certain. The 10-year rally got the headlines, but every large lender that reported this week guided to higher funding costs and most repriced their loans from 1 November. The market is pricing a bigger December RBI move through OIS, not a pause. Meanwhile banks lent 41.8% more to NBFCs than a year ago. That money is cheap and plentiful today, and RBI has shown before that it will slow it with risk weights.
